competencies.name: Neuron structural and functional classes
competencies.can: Classify a neuron as multipolar, bipolar, or pseudounipolar by structure and as sensory, motor, or interneuron by function, and match each class to a location in the nervous system.

competencies.name: Functional regions of a neuron
competencies.can: Label the dendrites, cell body, axon hillock, trigger zone, axon, and axon terminal and state which signal type each region carries.

competencies.name: Glial cell functions
competencies.can: Match astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia, ependymal cells, satellite cells, and Schwann cells to their physiological roles.

competencies.name: Myelin and its loss
competencies.can: Explain how myelin and the nodes of Ranvier speed conduction and predict the functional consequence of demyelination.

competencies.name: Axonal transport
competencies.can: Distinguish fast anterograde and retrograde axonal transport from slow transport and state what each carries.

competencies.name: Graded potentials
competencies.can: Describe how a graded potential is produced and explain why it varies with stimulus strength and decays with distance, using the terms current leak and cytoplasmic resistance.

competencies.name: Action potential phases
competencies.can: Diagram an action potential and state the channel state and ion movement responsible for depolarization to peak and for repolarization and afterhyperpolarization.

competencies.name: Threshold and all or none
competencies.can: Explain what threshold represents at the trigger zone and why action potential amplitude does not change with a stronger stimulus.

competencies.name: Coding of stimulus intensity
competencies.can: Explain how the nervous system encodes stimulus strength when action potential amplitude is fixed.

competencies.name: Refractory periods
competencies.can: Distinguish the absolute from the relative refractory period by channel state and explain how the refractory period sets maximum firing frequency and prevents backward conduction.

competencies.name: Conduction velocity
competencies.can: Rank axons by conduction velocity using diameter and myelination and contrast continuous with saltatory conduction.

competencies.name: Effects of altered extracellular ions
competencies.can: Predict the effect of hyperkalemia and hypokalemia on resting potential and excitability and explain why local anesthetics that block sodium channels abolish the action potential.

competencies.name: Action potential simulation
competencies.can: Run a neuron simulation with sodium and potassium channel blockers and interpret the resulting change in the action potential tracing.

competencies.name: Nerve conduction measurement
competencies.can: Measure conduction velocity from a recorded compound action potential and account for the difference between the fastest and slowest fibers.

competencies.name: Sequence at a chemical synapse
competencies.can: Order the events of chemical synaptic transmission from action potential arrival through calcium entry and vesicle fusion to receptor binding and postsynaptic response.

competencies.name: Neurotransmitter classes
competencies.can: Match acetylcholine, the catecholamines, serotonin, glutamate, GABA, glycine, and the neuropeptides to their usual excitatory or inhibitory effect and to a site of action.

competencies.name: Neurotransmitter removal
competencies.can: Name the three routes that clear a neurotransmitter from the synaptic cleft, degradation, reuptake, and diffusion, and give a drug that blocks one of them.

competencies.name: Excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic potentials
competencies.can: Distinguish an EPSP from an IPSP by the ion channel opened and the direction of the membrane potential change.

competencies.name: Summation and integration
competencies.can: Distinguish temporal from spatial summation and determine whether a stated combination of EPSPs and IPSPs will bring the trigger zone to threshold.

competencies.name: Presynaptic modulation
competencies.can: Compare presynaptic inhibition and facilitation with postsynaptic modulation and state the advantage of presynaptic control at a single input, which is selectivity.

competencies.name: Synaptic plasticity
competencies.can: Explain long term potentiation as a mechanism of learning and identify the roles of repeated stimulation and receptor insertion.

competencies.name: Electrical synapses
competencies.can: Compare an electrical synapse at a gap junction with a chemical synapse by speed and by capacity for modulation.

competencies.name: Synapse simulation
competencies.can: Alter neurotransmitter release and receptor availability in a synapse simulation and interpret the resulting postsynaptic recording.

competencies.name: Reflex arc components
competencies.can: Diagram a reflex arc naming the receptor, sensory neuron, integrating center, motor neuron, and effector, and classify the reflex as monosynaptic or polysynaptic.

competencies.name: Muscle spindle and stretch reflex
competencies.can: Explain how the muscle spindle detects stretch and trace the stretch reflex including reciprocal inhibition of the antagonist.

competencies.name: Golgi tendon organ
competencies.can: Contrast the stimulus and the reflex response of the Golgi tendon organ with those of the muscle spindle.

competencies.name: Withdrawal and crossed extensor reflexes
competencies.can: Trace the flexor withdrawal reflex and the crossed extensor reflex and explain how the two together preserve balance.

competencies.name: Ascending and descending pathways
competencies.can: Compare the dorsal column, spinothalamic, and corticospinal pathways by the information carried, the side of decussation, and the deficit produced by a lesion.

competencies.name: Cerebrospinal fluid and the blood brain barrier
competencies.can: State the functions of cerebrospinal fluid and explain how the blood brain barrier selects what reaches neurons, including why lipid soluble drugs cross readily.

competencies.name: Reflex testing and reaction time
competencies.can: Elicit and grade deep tendon reflexes and measure reaction time to distinguish a reflex response from a voluntary response by latency.

competencies.name: Neuromuscular junction
competencies.can: Trace transmission at the neuromuscular junction from the motor neuron action potential to the end plate potential and explain why every action potential in the motor neuron produces one in the muscle fiber.

competencies.name: Excitation contraction coupling
competencies.can: Trace excitation contraction coupling from the T tubule through the DHP and ryanodine receptors to calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.

competencies.name: Crossbridge cycle
competencies.can: Order the steps of the crossbridge cycle, binding, power stroke, detachment, and reactivation, and state where ATP binds and where it is hydrolyzed.

competencies.name: Calcium and the regulatory proteins
competencies.can: Explain how calcium binding to troponin moves tropomyosin off the myosin binding site and predict what happens to contraction if calcium cannot be released.

competencies.name: Relaxation and calcium removal
competencies.can: Explain how SERCA and acetylcholinesterase end a contraction and predict the result if either one fails.

competencies.name: The muscle twitch
competencies.can: Label the latent period, contraction phase, and relaxation phase on a twitch tracing and explain what limits each phase.

competencies.name: Summation and tetanus
competencies.can: Explain wave summation and distinguish unfused from fused tetanus by stimulus frequency and calcium accumulation.

competencies.name: Motor units and recruitment
competencies.can: Define the motor unit and explain how size of the unit and orderly recruitment grade the force a whole muscle produces.

competencies.name: Length tension relationship
competencies.can: Interpret a length tension curve and explain why tension falls at very short and very long sarcomere lengths.

competencies.name: Isometric and isotonic contraction
competencies.can: Distinguish isometric, concentric, and eccentric contractions and predict shortening velocity from the load applied.

competencies.name: Muscle fiber types
competencies.can: Compare slow oxidative, fast oxidative glycolytic, and fast glycolytic fibers by speed, ATP source, fatigue resistance, and typical task.

competencies.name: ATP sources during activity
competencies.can: Order creatine phosphate, anaerobic glycolysis, and oxidative phosphorylation by how quickly each supplies ATP and how long each can sustain it.

competencies.name: Fatigue and oxygen debt
competencies.can: Distinguish central from peripheral fatigue and explain the metabolic basis of excess post exercise oxygen consumption.

competencies.name: Muscle plasticity
competencies.can: Predict the change in fiber size, capillary supply, and mitochondrial content produced by endurance training, resistance training, and disuse.

competencies.name: Electromyography and grip fatigue
competencies.can: Record grip force and surface EMG over a sustained contraction and relate the decline in force to recruitment and fatigue.

competencies.name: Twitch and tetanus simulation
competencies.can: Generate twitch and tetanus tracings in a muscle simulation by varying stimulus voltage and frequency and identify threshold and maximal stimulus.

competencies.name: Smooth muscle contraction mechanism
competencies.can: Trace smooth muscle contraction through calcium entry and release to calmodulin and myosin light chain kinase and explain why the mechanism is slower and more economical than in skeletal muscle.

competencies.name: Smooth muscle types and regulation
competencies.can: Compare single unit and multi unit smooth muscle and list the stimuli that alter smooth muscle tone including stretch and local chemical signals.

competencies.name: Cardiac muscle properties
competencies.can: Explain how intercalated discs and gap junctions allow the myocardium to act as a functional syncytium and state why cardiac muscle cannot be tetanized.

competencies.name: Comparison of the three muscle types
competencies.can: Build a comparison of skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle by calcium source, regulatory protein, control, and speed of contraction.
